proposed_widenings.name: AnchorTarget.self
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's trigger is planted on the caster's person, not on a location or area. The existing AnchorTarget only admits { kind: 'location' } and { kind: 'area' }.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the contingent spell takes effect only on you... Contingency ends on you if its material component is ever not on your person

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredEvent.player_described_condition
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's trigger is an arbitrary natural-language condition described by the player at cast time ('when you are engulfed in water'). The existing AnchoredEvent only admits physical_contact and enters_area. An open player-described predicate cannot be modeled as a closed enum variant — it is structurally different from Alarm's fixed event vocabulary.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You describe that trigger when you cast the two spells. For example, a Contingency cast with Water Breathing might stipulate that Water Breathing comes into effect when you are engulfed in water or a similar liquid.

proposed_widenings.name: stored_spell (attachment)
proposed_widenings.justification: The contingent spell's payload is a full arbitrary spell (any spell level ≤5 that can target the caster, chosen at cast time). The output of the anchored trigger is not a closed AnchoredSignal (audible/mental notification) but a full stored spell that fires with its own effect atoms. The v4 taxonomy lists 'stored_spell' as an attachment atom but it is absent from types.ts.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast, that has a casting time of an action, and that can target you. You cast that spell—called the contingent spell—as part of casting Contingency, expending spell slots for both, but the contingent spell doesn't come into effect. Instead, it takes effect when a certain trigger occurs.

proposed_widenings.name: SpellMechanicsHeader.dualSlotCost
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency consumes two spell slots simultaneously at cast time: the Contingency slot (level 6) and the contingent spell's slot (level ≤5, player-chosen). No existing surface shape expresses a cast that consumes a second variable-level spell slot as part of activation.

proposed_widenings.name: one_at_a_time exclusion / recasting ends prior
proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency explicitly ends any prior Contingency when recast. The existing DurationEndTrigger variants (target_makes_attack_roll, target_deals_damage, target_casts_spell, target_dons_armor, target_damaged_by_caster_or_ally, target_takes_damage, caster_recasts_spell) include caster_recasts_spell which covers the recast case. However the material-component-must-be-on-person clause is not representable as any existing end trigger.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Contingency ends on you if its material component is ever not on your person.

notes: Contingency is structurally closest to anchored_trigger but differs in three fundamental ways: (1) the anchor is 'self' (caster's person), not a location or area; (2) the trigger is a player-described freeform condition, not a closed enum event; (3) the output is a stored arbitrary spell, not an audible/mental signal. The v4 taxonomy already names 'stored_spell' as an attachment atom and 'store'/'release' as procedure atoms, but these are absent from types.ts. Additionally, the dual-slot expenditure (Contingency slot + contingent spell slot) has no surface representation. No honest encoding is possible under the current surface.
